name: Principal-Protected Note Replication
summary: The desk build of a structured note: a zero-coupon-equivalent bond position sized to return full principal at the horizon, with the discount spent on a call spread that defines the participation band.

legs.strike_rule: Treasury sleeve (SGOV/BIL, or a specific-maturity Treasury ETF matching the horizon) sized so sleeve x (1 + yield x years) = the principal to be protected
ATM on SPY or QQQ, call delta 0.50
OTM at the participation cap, call delta 0.20-0.30; strike solved so the spread's cost equals the bond discount
legs.dte_rule: same expiry as the long call

max_profit: (cap strike - long strike - net debit) x 100 per unit, plus full principal returned by the sleeve
max_loss: The net debit only - i.e. the interest forgone. Principal is returned by the bond sleeve at the horizon.
breakevens: long call strike + net debit per share on the option sleeve; the portfolio itself breaks even flat

greeks.gamma: small, positive near the long strike
greeks.theta: negative on the spread, offset by bond accrual

typical_dte: 180-365 DTE, matched to the protection horizon
when_to_use: When a fixed horizon and a hard capital floor are both required - the exact thing a bank sells as a principal-protected note, built for the cost of two option legs instead of a 2% structuring fee. Requires a yield environment where the discount actually buys a meaningful spread; at sub-2% yields the cap is too low to bother.
entry_rules: Define the horizon H in days and the principal P to protect before anything is bought.
Sleeve size = P / (1 + y x H/365) where y is the current yield on the matching Treasury maturity. The residual (P minus sleeve size) is the entire option budget.
Option budget must buy a call spread whose cap is at least 8% above spot; if it cannot, the environment does not support this structure - do not compromise the floor to widen the cap.
Both call legs same expiry, expiry >= H, on SPY or QQQ only, OI >= 250 each, single MLeg order.
Short call strike must be above the long call strike by design; the short is fully covered by the long, which keeps this at level 3.
Re-check that total option debit <= the bond discount before submission; a debit larger than the discount breaks the protection.
management_rules: Hold the spread to within 10 days of the horizon; this is not a trade to manage, it is a payoff to deliver.
Optional early monetization: if the spread reaches 80% of its maximum value with more than 60 days left, close it and move the proceeds to the sleeve - the structure has delivered its cap early.
Never sell the bond sleeve to add to the option spread.
Reconstitute annually with the new yield, which sets the new cap.
exit_rules: Close both call legs at least 2 trading days before expiration; never allow the long call to auto-exercise into shares or the short call to be assigned.
Close the short call immediately if its extrinsic < $0.10 or delta >= 0.85 (leaving the long call alone), and before any ex-dividend date while it is ITM.
At the horizon, redeem the sleeve to cash and report the realized participation against the cap.
assignment_risk: One short call, covered by a long call at a lower strike, so any assignment is defined - but assignment delivers a 100-share short position that must be closed by exercising the long. The pre-expiry close rule is what prevents it.
buying_power: Sleeve cash plus the spread's net debit; the short call is covered by the long, so no separate requirement.
liquidity_needs: Treasury ETFs are penny-wide; the long-dated SPY/QQQ spread must be closeable as one ticket.
common_mistakes: Sizing the sleeve off today's principal instead of the discounted value, which leaves the floor short; buying an uncapped long call with the discount and calling it protected when the premium exceeds the discount; mismatching the option expiry to the horizon.
family: Completeness gap-fill (cross-family): ratio/naked-financed put and call structures, quantity-unbalanced condors and strangles, stock+option overlays and monetizations, capital-protection and hybrid builds, 0DTE four-leg income, volatility-surface and relative-value trades, event-driven overlays, and roll/adjustment structures
